title: Egypt Starts Gas Production at the Mediterranean Mina West Field, High Energy Costs Push Japan's Economy Into a Q3 Contraction, and Asia Builds 73% of New Global Nuclear Capacity
subhead: Egypt and Shell launched natural gas production at the Mediterranean Mina West field with a daily capacity of 160 million cubic feet as crude oil prices eased on US-Iran ceasefire hopes; elevated war-driven energy prices pushed Japan's economy into an unexpected third-quarter contraction after subsidies expired; and new data showed Asia accounts for 73 percent of global nuclear power construction.

sections.heading: Egypt Starts Gas Production at the Mediterranean Mina West Field as Oil Eases on US-Iran Deal Hopes
sections.body:
Anadolu Agency, CNA, and Wall Street Journal — Egypt's Ministry of Petroleum and energy major Shell announced the start of natural gas production at the new Mina West offshore field in the Mediterranean Sea, a development expected to supply up to 160 million standard cubic feet of gas per day to Egypt's domestic energy market (Anadolu Agency). The new Mediterranean supply comes as Cairo seeks to curb costly liquefied natural gas imports and stabilize domestic power generation ahead of peak winter demand.

In global oil markets, benchmark crude prices edged lower in early Monday trading as forecasts of a coming 2027 supply surplus and signals from Tehran that the path to a US ceasefire deal remains open tempered war-risk premiums (CNA, Wall Street Journal, Bloomberg). Supporting the softer price outlook, the US Energy Information Administration projected that global liquid fuels production will return to pre-Iran-war levels by the end of the year as non-OPEC supply expands (EnergyNow).
sections.whyItMatters: Bringing 160 million cubic feet per day online at Mina West helps Egypt reduce its reliance on spot LNG cargoes while global crude traders weigh ceasefire prospects against Gulf shipping risks.

sections.heading: Elevated Iran-War Energy Costs Push Japan's Economy Into an Unexpected Third-Quarter Contraction as China's Output Slows
sections.body:
CNBC and Hürriyet Daily News — Japan's gross domestic product unexpectedly contracted in the third quarter of 2026 as elevated crude oil and liquefied natural gas import costs resulting from the Iran conflict weighed heavily on household consumption and industrial margins, CNBC reported Monday. Economists noted that Tokyo's utility and fuel subsidies for households expired in September, directly exposing Japanese consumers to higher energy bills during the autumn quarter.

In neighboring China—the world's largest crude oil importer—economic momentum also weakened in October as industrial output, retail sales, and fixed-asset investment all missed market expectations amid a five-year property downturn (CNBC). Elsewhere among major energy producers, Hürriyet Daily News reported that Russia's economic growth slowed to 1 percent in the third quarter as sanctions, high interest rates, and labor shortages constrained non-military output.
sections.whyItMatters: Japan's third-quarter GDP contraction provides the clearest macroeconomic evidence yet of how eight months of Middle East energy disruptions are eroding growth in resource-importing Asian economies.

sections.heading: Asia Accounts for 73% of the World's New Nuclear Power Construction as Middle East Energy Disruptions Bite
sections.body:
OilPrice and Anadolu Agency — Asian nations are now building 73 percent of all new nuclear power generation capacity under construction globally, OilPrice reported, as the Middle East conflict and recurring Strait of Hormuz shipping bottlenecks compel governments from China and India to Southeast Asia to prioritize domestic baseload electricity over imported fossil fuels. The nuclear construction surge is running in parallel with rapid solar, wind, and grid-storage deployment across ASEAN member states seeking to insulate their power grids from volatile LNG and coal import bills.

In regional electricity markets, Anadolu Agency reported that Turkey's daily power consumption declined by 5 percent on November 14 amid milder autumn temperatures and strong domestic wind generation. Meanwhile, at the UN COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Brazil launched two international roadmaps offering national planning templates to accelerate the global phase-out of fossil fuels (OilPrice).
sections.whyItMatters: With Asia building nearly three-quarters of the world's new nuclear reactors, the center of gravity for nuclear supply chains, fuel enrichment, and reactor financing has shifted firmly eastward.

sections.heading: US Oil Producers Reap a $130B Boom From the Iran War as North Dakota Crude Output Rises
sections.body:
OilPrice, EnergyNow, and Reuters — United States oil, natural gas, and refined-product companies have reaped an estimated $130 billion export windfall since the outbreak of the Iran war in February as European and Asian refiners turned to American barrels to replace disrupted Persian Gulf shipments, OilPrice reported. Despite the export boom, US domestic fuel politics remain heated, with President Donald Trump demanding that major oil companies lower retail gasoline prices and publicly rebuking Chevron's chief executive (EnergyNow).

In US upstream production, North Dakota regulators projected that Bakken shale crude output will rise in the months ahead as operators capitalize on sustained high oil prices (EnergyNow). Along the US Gulf Coast export corridor, the National Transportation Safety Board announced that a steering system failure aboard a commercial tanker caused last week's collision with a riverboat in New Orleans that hospitalized 32 people (Reuters).
sections.whyItMatters: The $130 billion US energy export boom highlights the widening divergence between American hydrocarbon producers profiting from wartime trade rerouting and Asian and European importers absorbing the cost.

sections.heading: Electric Vehicles Cut Global Fuel Demand in 2025 as Western Australia Mining Hits Record Jobs
sections.body:
InsideEVs, OilPrice, and Reuters — Expanding electric vehicle fleets displaced a record volume of global road-fuel consumption in 2025, InsideEVs reported, demonstrating lasting demand erosion in gasoline and diesel markets even as wartime geopolitical risks keep spot crude prices elevated. In industrial metals, however, benchmark copper prices entered the week after five consecutive weekly declines as traders weighed whether leadership turmoil at Nvidia will slow hyperscaler AI data-center power and wiring investments (OilPrice).

Upstream in the critical minerals supply chain, industry data showed Western Australia's mining and resources sector generated record employment alongside a strong multi-year project development queue (Mining.com.au). In precious metals, spot gold edged higher on Monday morning as institutional investors awaited interest-rate signals from Federal Reserve officials and monitored Singapore's newly opened 500-ton sovereign bullion vault (Reuters, OilPrice).
sections.whyItMatters: Record fuel displacement from electric vehicles alongside softer Chinese industrial data explains why energy agencies expect the global oil market to tip back into surplus once Gulf shipping normalizes.

bottomLine: Monday's energy developments illustrate the dual reality of the 2026 market: while eight months of Iran-war disruptions have handed US oil exporters a $130 billion boom, pushed Japan's economy into a third-quarter contraction, and driven Asia to build 73 percent of the world's new nuclear reactors, rising non-OPEC crude supply, Egypt's new Mina West gas field, and growing EV fuel displacement are already laying the groundwork for a post-war supply surplus.
